name: Materials — coal_mining_industrial_production covariate forecasting bundle (monthly)
citation: FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis); Yahoo Finance (yfinance)
license: FRED: public data redistributed under FRED terms of use; Yahoo Finance: personal/research use per Yahoo terms.
description: Non-EIA, non-benchmark macro/market sources. FRED Industrial Production & PPI indices and Yahoo futures closes are not part of any forecasting-benchmark training corpus, avoiding target leakage. Long-format TempusBench bundle for application 'covariate_materials_monthly_coal_mining_output'. Target 'coal_mining_industrial_production' forecast from 6 covariates. monthly cadence, 310 timesteps, 2000-08-01..2026-05-01. NON-EIA (the foundation model is EIA-trained, so EIA sources are excluded). eia_derived=false.
preprocessing: 1. Pull 5 FRED monthly series (IPN2121N, IPG2122N, PCU21212121, IPMINE, IPB50001N) via keyless fredgraph.csv; cache raw CSV.
2. Parse FRED CSV; coerce '.' missing markers to NaN; drop leading/trailing NaN; normalize observation_date to month-start timestamps.
3. Download NG=F and HG=F daily history via yfinance (auto_adjust=True); cache raw daily CSV.
4. Resample each futures Close to monthly LAST close, stamp at month start.
5. Inner-join all 7 series on the month-start date key (common overlap).
6. Linear-interpolate small internal gaps (<=3 consecutive, interior only).
7. Add month_num from the date index (known-future calendar covariate).
8. Order columns (date, targets, covariates); dedupe boundary duplicates; drop residual NaN; assert monotonic-unique index and zero NaN.
9. Write wide tidy CSV with 'YYYY-MM-01' labels and meta.json provenance.
10. Reformatted wide->long TempusBench (variable_name, variable_unit, timestamps, values); timestamps ISO-8601 UTC; variable names expanded; missing->null; values round-trip-verified against source.
11. Removed calendar/time covariates (month_of_year) from the CSV so the only representation of time is the shared 'timestamps' column.

12. Variable names are written in plain English (underscores replaced with spaces). Target — 'coal mining industrial production' (from source column 'coal_ip_nsa', unit: index (2017=100)). Covariates — 'metal ore mining industrial production' (from source column 'metalore_ip_nsa', unit: index (2017=100)); 'coal mining producer price index' (from source column 'coal_ppi', unit: index); 'total mining industrial production' (from source column 'mining_ip', unit: index (2017=100)); 'total industrial production' (from source column 'total_ip', unit: index (2017=100)); 'henry hub natural gas front month settlement' (from source column 'natgas_close', unit: USD/MMBtu); 'comex copper front month settlement' (from source column 'copper_close', unit: USD/pound).

13. Added binary calendar covariates 'is weekend', 'is holiday' (0/1), derived deterministically from the shared 'timestamps' (weekend = Sat/Sun; holiday = US federal holidays). This bundle is monthly (timestamps are month-start dates), so these day-level flags reflect only the 1st of each month and merely reflect the calendar status of that single first-of-month date, not the month as a whole (uninformative here).
14. Removed the calendar covariates 'is weekend' and 'is holiday' from the delivered CSV.
